The Journal of Antibiotics, Series A Online ISSN : 2435-5135 Print ISSN : 0368-1173 ISSN-L : 0368-1173 Clinical Studies on Danomycin, with Reference to Laboratory Tests Ryochi Fujii, Masatoshi Konno, Masanori Takeshita Author information * Ryochi Fujii Department of Pediatrics, Tokyo University Branch Hospital * Masatoshi Konno Department of Pediatrics, Tokyo University Branch Hospital * Masanori Takeshita Department of Pediatrics, Tokyo University Branch Hospital #### Corresponding author Image: ORCID JOURNAL FREE ACCESS 1964 Volume 17 Issue 2 Pages 57-64 DOI https://doi.org/10.11554/antibioticsa.17.2_57 Details * Published: 1964 Received: September 05, 1963 Available on J-STAGE: July 07, 2020 Accepted: - Advance online publication: - Revised: - Download PDF (14063K) Article overview * Abstract * References (6) * Content from these authors Abstract Danomycin^{1)}, a product from a strain of Streptomyces albaduncus nov. sp., is a watersoluble antibiotic, orange red in color, and containing iron molecules in its polypeptide structure. Danomycin is effective in vitro against Gram-positive organisms such as Staphylococcus aureus and Pneumococccus, while ineffective against Staphylococcus albus, Streptococcus hemolyticus as well as Gram-negative bacteria. Because of the high incidence of staphylococcal infections in infancy and young childhood, our concerns have been chiefly about danomycin with its clinical effect on staphylococcal infections. In vitro sensitivities of coagulase-positive staphylococci to danomycin and other several antibiotics, the blood levels and the urinary excretions of danomycin in children, and its clinical effects including the side effects have been studied. The present report deals with our results obtained.
